title: What Our Top Customers Do Differently: Your 2027 Setup Checklist
summary: Our CSMs shared what their highest-performing accounts do differently. Here's the recap, plus six steps to get Ambition ready before January.
body_markdown:
*Our CSMs shared what their highest-performing accounts do differently. Here's the recap, plus six steps to get Ambition ready before January.*


Last month's Coach to Close was about the Q4 finish line: hitting the number without burning out your team. This month, we zoomed out. We asked our Customer Success Managers a simple question: when you look at your highest-performing accounts, what are they doing that everyone else can repeat?


The answer wasn't a feature list. Ryan Logan, one of Ambition's Customer Success Managers, put it this way: success with Ambition isn't tied to how many features a team uses. It's tied to the habits they've built around the platform. How involved are their leaders? How much do their teams trust the data? And how much of their week actually runs through Ambition?


Below, we cover what those top customers do, how to bring those habits to your own team, and the 2027 setup checklist we walked through at the end of the session.


# **What Top Customers Do Differently**


The same three habits came up again and again: leaders own it from the top, their data is trusted, and Ambition runs their daily rhythm.


### **Leaders Own It From the Top**


At our most successful customers, Ambition isn't owned by one admin or a lone champion. There's real alignment at the leadership level, and leaders understand the why behind the platform. Three examples:


- **A national telecom** pairs strong enablement leadership with sales leadership. Both sides believe coaching is fundamental to hitting the number, so they dedicated resources to it, built a structured coaching process, and partner closely with our CX team to keep managers and sellers aligned.
- **A payroll and HR provider's** digital sales team runs on Ambition. Reps, managers, and VPs all use it for accountability, visibility, recognition, and competition, and their end-user adoption is among our highest, year over year.
- **A global software company** had the right people in the room from day one, including business owners and someone who knows their data inside out. That's what lets them scale.


When alignment exists at the top, adoption gets a lot easier everywhere else.


### **Their Data Is Trusted**


This is the one Ryan can't emphasize enough. You can have the best scorecards, competitions, and coaching programs configured, but if managers and sellers don't trust the numbers underneath them, adoption stalls. Top customers do three things well:


1. **Set the rules first.** They agree on one way to identify reps, which metrics matter, and how each one is defined, before anything gets built.
2. **Validate early.** They compare what's in Ambition against their source of truth before reps ever see it.
3. **Fix it together.** When a number looks off, they dig in with our team to understand why, instead of assuming the platform is wrong.


The goal: managers spend their one-on-ones talking about how to improve performance, not debating whether the data is accurate.


### **Ambition Runs the Daily Rhythm**


Top customers don't just log in at the end of the month to see who hit quota. They use Ambition to run recurring one-on-ones, monitor performance through the week, recognize wins, and step in before small gaps turn into big ones.


They also balance standards with flexibility. Leaders set clear expectations for what coaching looks like, then give managers room to tailor conversations to each seller. Consistency doesn't mean every conversation looks the same. It means a repeatable framework that still lets managers coach their way.


Two examples of what that looks like in practice:


- **A lending company** runs a monthly manager cadence, holds regular executive syncs with our team, and tracks coaching completion %.
- **A logistics company's** leaders bought in early and stayed visible. Log-in % is the number they watch to see who's engaged.


Different business models, same move: both teams measure the habits that drive performance, not only the results.


### **They Grew Into the Platform**


Many of our top customers didn't start out using everything. A waste services company came to us for scorecards, TVs, and competitions. As that foundation matured, coaching became the natural next step, tying performance data to development conversations. Now they want to go deeper on pipeline and forecasting. A digital marketing company followed the same path, starting with visibility and recognition, then expanding while pushing our product team with feedback along the way.


The takeaway: you don't have to do everything at once. Start with the business problem you're solving, build a strong foundation, and expand when your team is ready.


## **Bring It to Your Team**


Knowing what top customers do is the easy part. Here's how to put those habits to work on your own team heading into 2027.


### **Start at the Top**


There's a real difference between positioning Ambition as a way to track metrics and positioning it as the answer to a business problem. If it's just another tool in a rep's tech stack, buy-in is hard to sustain. Tie it to a priority your org already feels, like quota attainment, manager consistency, pipeline generation, or accountability, and the conversation changes.


Ryan's recommendation: name an executive sponsor who can clearly say why Ambition matters to the business, then make sure sales and enablement leaders agree on what success looks like. If adoption is stalling, ask your champions one question: does our org understand *why* we use Ambition, or do they just know they're supposed to?


### **Build One Version of the Truth**


Before Ambition, many teams have their own reports, managers define the same KPI differently, and results get debated in meetings. The goal is the opposite: everyone agrees on which metrics matter, how each is measured, and where to find them.


One logistics carrier pulls revenue from seven different systems, so they set one unique ID for every rep at the source. When a rep's number was questioned, their BI lead rebuilt it himself from the source data, and it matched Ambition exactly. That's what data trust looks like in practice.


Before January, sit down with your business stakeholders, RevOps team, and data owners to revisit your metric definitions. Make sure every number is accurate, relevant, and tied to the behaviors you want to drive in 2027.


### **Make It the Carrot, Not the Stick**


One of Ryan's favorite customer stories comes from a debt relief company. Their team asked for a "wasted time" metric, where a lower number meant better performance. Their product owner pushed back: "I think of Ambition as the carrot, not the stick."


So they used the Formula Builder to flip it into **productive time** , a number reps work to raise. Same business goal, but now reps had something to work toward and feel good about improving.


**Try it:** pick one metric your team gets penalized on, and turn it into one they can win.


### **Make Coaching a Habit**


We asked how often your managers run one-on-ones today, and the answers covered every option, from weekly to whenever there's time. There's no single right answer. Different teams and roles need different cadences.


What matters is a clear expectation that coaching happens consistently, with accountability coming out of every conversation. Managers should walk in knowing where performance stands, leave with actionable next steps, and follow up on those commitments next time. That's when coaching stops being a meeting on the calendar and becomes an ongoing development process.


### **Six Plays to Try**


1. **Name an exec sponsor.** Pair a sales leader with an enablement lead who can say what Ambition is there to do.
2. **Get the right people in the room.** Include someone who knows your business processes and your data from day one.
3. **Write your data rules down.** One way to identify reps, plus agreed metric definitions.
4. **Validate before reps see it.** Building trust up front pays off when it's time for adoption.
5. **Give managers a template, not a script.** Set the standard, then let managers make coaching their own.
6. **Put coaching on the calendar.** Set a recurring cadence and track whether it's actually happening.


You don't need to tackle all six at once. Pick the one or two where your team has the most room to grow, and make those your January priorities.


## **Self-Check: Where Does Your Team Stand?**


Before building your January plan, take a quick gut check. Ask yourself whether each of these is a yes or a not yet for your team:


- We have an exec owner who can say why Ambition matters.
- Our data rules are written down.
- Numbers are validated before reps see them.
- Managers coach on a recurring cadence, and we track completion.
- The people who know our business and data are involved.
- Managers have a coaching template they can adapt.


Count your "not yets." Those are your first plays for January. The ones you can already say yes to can wait. There's always room to improve, but the not-yets are where you have the most to gain over the next month and a half.


## **Your 2027 Setup Checklist**


This is where everything above turns into action. Here's how we'd pace it:


- **Late November:** clean up users and groups, and write down your 2027 data rules.
- **December:** validate metrics against your source of truth, then publish 2027 scorecards and targets.
- **January:** start your Q1 coaching cadence and launch a kickoff win.


#### **1. Clean Up Users & Groups for 2027 Teams**


The simplest advice we hear from our CSMs: pick one way to identify reps and stick to it. Then:


- **Reflect 2027 reorgs.** Move people to their new teams and managers before January 1.
- **Add new hires.** Invite them now so they start the year on a scorecard.
- **Archive people who've left,** so rollups and leaderboards stay accurate.


Do this now, and you won't come back from the holidays feeling behind.


#### **2. Write Down Your 2027 Data Rules**


If comp plans, territories, or metric definitions are changing, write them down early. Then update your metrics to match, using the same filters as the reports your managers already trust.


#### **3. Validate Metrics Against Your Source of Truth**


Before reps ever see a number, compare each metric to the report it should match. If something's off, you'll catch it early and work through it with us, instead of building distrust into your rollout.


#### **4. Publish 2027 Scorecards & Targets**


For scorecards:


- Choose 3–5 metrics per team.
- Start with metrics you've already validated.
- If scorecards are new for your team, launch with one team, then roll out.


For targets:


- Base them on your imported history.
- Match the goals managers already share with their teams.
- Check that team totals add up in rollups.


A reminder from last month: **Calculate Target** in your scorecard settings looks at your last 12 weeks of real data and sets a target for you. It's an easy starting point that reflects what your team has actually been capable of.


#### **5. Schedule Your Q1 Coaching Cadence**


Whether your managers already run weekly one-on-ones or are still working toward a goal, get the motions in place now:


- **Set a recurring one-on-one cadence,** weekly or every other week, decided team by team.
- **Schedule sessions inside coaching programs** with real meeting times for each participant. The **calendar integration** syncs both ways with Google or Microsoft calendars. Your admin connects it first, then each user authorizes their own calendar. Check sessions against the PTO logged in Ambition so they actually happen.
- **Track coaching completion %** and review it in a monthly leadership sync, like our top customers do.


#### **6. Plan a January 1st Win**


Pick one of these and put it on the calendar for your first week back:


- **Launch a kickoff competition.** One metric your team rallies around, one or two weeks long. It's an easy way to get everyone fired up.
- **Schedule a workflow.** A recurring nudge on a rhythm your team already follows, like Monday mornings. If you're already using **scheduled Skills,** this is a great place for one, delivered to you automatically.
- **Run a coaching session.** Review the rep's scorecard first, then capture next steps together.


The best part: you can lay all this groundwork now. When you come back in January, everything is ready, and you can dive right in instead of starting the year behind.


### **If You Do Nothing Else**


1. Clean up users & groups for 2027 teams.
2. Write down your 2027 data rules.
3. Validate metrics against your source of truth.
4. Publish 2027 scorecards & targets.
5. Schedule your Q1 coaching cadence.
6. Plan a January 1st win.


None of these are huge lifts on their own. And because everything in Ambition builds on everything else, even tackling two or three of them will make the rest easier.
